and review at the Public Works Yard located at 124 S. Lake Street.

This facility is disabled accessible. In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA), if any
special assistance is needed to participate in this meeting, please contact the City’s ADA Coordinator at
(818) 238-5051 (voice) or (818) 238-5035 TDD. Advance notification of 48 hours will permit the City to
make reasonable accommodations to ensure accessibility.

 STAFF REPORT

  COMMUNITY
  DEVELOPMENT

DATE:  September 21, 2026

TO:  Sustainable Burbank Commission

FROM:  Fred Ramirez, Assistant Community Development Director - Planning
  Via: Scott Plambaeck, Planning Manager
  By:  Leonard Bechet, Principal Planner

SUBJECT: Status Report on the Downtown Transit Oriented Development Specific
  Plan

RECOMMENDATION
Receive an update on the Draft Downtown Transit Oriented Development Specific Plan.

BACKGROUND
The Downtown Burbank Transit Oriented Development Specific Plan (Downtown TOD
Specific Plan or Specific Plan) is a new planning document that establishes a coordinated
policy framework, unified land-use vision, and objective development standards to guide
future growth and reinvestment within the 918-acre Plan Area in Downtown Burbank
(Downtown). Replacing the 1997 Burbank Center Plan and the 2012 North San Fernando
Boulevard Master Plan, the Specific Plan builds on these earlier efforts by addressing the
City’s housing needs at all affordability levels through infill development of housing
opportunity sites, updated zoning regulations to incentivize public and private investment,
and new placemaking opportunities that include the redevelopment of the Burbank Town
Center and City Civic Center areas. Additionally, the Specific Plan promotes complete
streets and improved connectivity through a unified vision for Downtown.

Development of the Downtown TOD Specific Plan is funded through the following
sources:
  • Los Angeles County Metropolitan Transit Authority (METRO) – Transit Oriented
  Development Planning Grant Program
   •  California Department of Housing and Community Development (HCD) – SB 2
  Planning Grant Program
  •  City General Funds (previously authorized by City Council)

DISCUSSION
Staff have prepared a draft of the Specific Plan and have made it available for public
review. The draft Specific Plan contains objective standards consistent with recent state
housing legislation, providing clear guidance for qualifying projects while maintaining as
much local discretion as allowed under current law. The draft Specific Plan is organized
into ten chapters and includes a guide for navigating the document. Summaries of each
chapter are provided below. Appendices are currently being finalized and will be included
in the final draft.

  1. Introduction (Page 8 of Attachment 1)
  Describes the purpose of the Specific Plan, its legal authority, and its relationship
  to other City plans and policies.

  2. Background and Context (Page 15 of Attachment 1)
  Summarizes existing conditions, demographic trends, and other factors that inform
  the plan's vision, policies, and implementation measures.

  3. Vision, Goals, and Policies (Page 24 of Attachment 1)
  Presents the community vision and establishes the goals and policies that will
  guide future development in Downtown Burbank. This chapter reflects the
  community’s aspirations for how they envision Downtown’s transformation over the
  next decade.

  4. Urban Design, Land Use, and Housing (Page 36 of Attachment 1)
  Establishes land use goals, policies, and designations for the Specific Plan area.

  5. Public Realm (Page 52 of Attachment 1)
  Outlines strategies for enhancing streets, parks, plazas, and open spaces to
  support a walkable, attractive, and transit-oriented downtown environment.

  6. Circulation and Mobility (Page 59 of Attachment 1)
  Establishes mobility policies and identifies improvements to support safe and
  efficient travel for pedestrians, bicyclists, transit users, and motorists, consistent
  with the Complete Our Streets Plan that was adopted by City Council in 2020.

  2
   7. Parking (Page 93 of Attachment 1)
  Provides strategies for managing parking, including shared parking, unbundled
  parking, expansion of the Central Business District Parking Area, and other parking
  management tools.

  8. Utilities and Infrastructure (Page 104 of Attachment 1)
  Addresses existing and planned utility and infrastructure systems needed to
  support future development. This chapter will be expanded following completion
  and public review of the Draft Program EIR.

  9. Development Code (Page 105 of Attachment 1)
  Establishes land use regulations, permitted uses, development standards, design
  guidelines, transfer of development rights provisions, community benefits, and
  other objective standards necessary to implement the Specific Plan.

  10. Implementation (Page 187 of Attachment 1)
  Identifies the regulatory actions, programs, capital improvements, and financing
  strategies needed to implement the Specific Plan. This chapter will be refined
  following completion and public review of the Draft Program EIR.

COMMUNITY OUTREACH
Community engagement has been a central component of the Downtown TOD Specific
Plan process, supported by workshops, walking tours, surveys, stakeholder interviews,
and coordination with City boards and commissions. Staff held a City Council study
session on June 30, 2026, where the draft Plan was released for public review. Members
of the community have already begun providing feedback to the draft specific plan, and
Staff will incorporate this feedback into a final plan. Two community open houses were
conducted on August 30 and September 2, 2026, with additional outreach continuing
through Summer and Fall 2026.

Public involvement will expand further with the release of the Draft Program EIR in Fall
2026, including public notice, a 45-day review period, and a Planning Commission
meeting. Additional opportunities for comment will occur during Planning Commission and
City Council consideration of the Specific Plan and Program EIR.

ENVIRONMENTAL ASSESSMENT
The Downtown TOD Specific Plan is subject to CEQA, and the City is preparing a
Program EIR, supported by two years of technical studies evaluating infrastructure
capacity and potential impacts, including electrical, water, wastewater, and transportation

  3
 systems. Because the City is preparing the Downtown TOD, Golden State, and Media
District Specific Plans concurrently, each study includes cumulative analysis, with a
similar review planned for the Burbank Rancho Neighborhood Specific Plan. These
studies will streamline future project-level environmental review, identify needed
infrastructure improvements, inform objective development standards and fees, and
guide future capital and adequate public facilities planning. Preparation of the Program
EIR will continue through Summer 2026, with the Draft Program EIR anticipated for public
release in Fall 2026.

CONCLUSION
The Downtown TOD Specific Plan provides a comprehensive framework to guide future
growth, housing production, mobility improvements, public investment, and neighborhood
preservation in Downtown. The plan is intended to help the City comply with evolving
state housing requirements while maintaining a clear local vision for development. As
previously noted, additional public outreach, environmental review, and plan refinement
will continue throughout 2026. Staff is seeking feedback from the Sustainable Burbank
Commission to ensure the plan aligns with community priorities and objectives. Additional
public outreach, environmental review, and plan refinement will continue throughout 2026
before the plan is presented to the Planning Commission and City Council for
consideration in Winter 2027.
